    // The diamond cubic cell: four interior nodes at the quarter points, each
    // bonded tetrahedrally to one corner and three face centers. Coordination 4
    // everywhere. Four of the eight corners carry no strut inside this cell;
    // they are listed because the tiling needs a node on every cube corner, and
    // once tiled all eight are the same welded node.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_cubic)
    DiamondCubic(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(
            LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners
                .Concatenate(LatticeUnitCell.CubeFaceCenters)
                .Concatenate([
                    Point3D(0.25, 0.25, 0.25), Point3D(0.75, 0.75, 0.25),
                    Point3D(0.75, 0.25, 0.75), Point3D(0.25, 0.75, 0.75)
                ]),
            [
                Strut(14, 0), Strut(14, 8), Strut(14, 10), Strut(14, 12),
                Strut(15, 2), Strut(15, 8), Strut(15, 11), Strut(15, 13),
                Strut(16, 5), Strut(16, 9), Strut(16, 10), Strut(16, 13),
                Strut(17, 7), Strut(17, 9), Strut(17, 11), Strut(17, 12)
            ]);

    // The Kelvin cell: the wireframe of a truncated octahedron (a
    // tetrakaidecahedron), whose six square faces sit exactly on the cube faces
    // and are therefore shared with the neighbouring cells. Coordination 4 once
    // tiled, though the polyhedron itself is 3-valent: the fourth strut comes
    // from the neighbour across the square face. This is Kelvin's answer to the
    // minimal-surface foam problem.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truncated_octahedron)
    TruncatedOctahedron(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(
            [
                Point3D(0.0, 0.25, 0.5), Point3D(0.0, 0.5, 0.25),
                Point3D(0.0, 0.5, 0.75), Point3D(0.0, 0.75, 0.5),
                Point3D(0.25, 0.0, 0.5), Point3D(0.25, 0.5, 0.0),
                Point3D(0.25, 0.5, 1.0), Point3D(0.25, 1.0, 0.5),
                Point3D(0.5, 0.0, 0.25), Point3D(0.5, 0.0, 0.75),
                Point3D(0.5, 0.25, 0.0), Point3D(0.5, 0.25, 1.0),
                Point3D(0.5, 0.75, 0.0), Point3D(0.5, 0.75, 1.0),
                Point3D(0.5, 1.0, 0.25), Point3D(0.5, 1.0, 0.75),
                Point3D(0.75, 0.0, 0.5), Point3D(0.75, 0.5, 0.0),
                Point3D(0.75, 0.5, 1.0), Point3D(0.75, 1.0, 0.5),
                Point3D(1.0, 0.25, 0.5), Point3D(1.0, 0.5, 0.25),
                Point3D(1.0, 0.5, 0.75), Point3D(1.0, 0.75, 0.5)
            ],
            [
                Strut(0, 1), Strut(0, 2), Strut(0, 4), Strut(1, 3),
                Strut(1, 5), Strut(2, 3), Strut(2, 6), Strut(3, 7),
                Strut(4, 8), Strut(4, 9), Strut(5, 10), Strut(5, 12),
                Strut(6, 11), Strut(6, 13), Strut(7, 14), Strut(7, 15),
                Strut(8, 10), Strut(8, 16), Strut(9, 11), Strut(9, 16),
                Strut(10, 17), Strut(11, 18), Strut(12, 14), Strut(12, 17),
                Strut(13, 15), Strut(13, 18), Strut(14, 19), Strut(15, 19),
                Strut(16, 20), Strut(17, 21), Strut(18, 22), Strut(19, 23),
                Strut(20, 21), Strut(20, 22), Strut(21, 23), Strut(22, 23)
            ]);

    // The three-dimensional re-entrant honeycomb, the standard auxetic cell: the
    // twelve cube edges each replaced by a two-segment rib that folds INWARD by
    // `reentrancy` at its midpoint. Stretching the cell along an axis unfolds
    // those ribs and pushes the other axes outward, which is the negative
    // Poisson ratio (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auxetics). The corner nodes
    // reach coordination 24; the twelve rib nodes are 2-valent hinges, which is
    // the mechanism and not a defect. `reentrancy` of 0 collapses the cell back
    // to `SimpleCubic` with each edge split in two; useful values are well below
    // 0.5, where opposite ribs would meet.
    ReentrantHoneycomb(reentrancy: Number): LatticeUnitCell
    {
        var r = reentrancy;
        var s = 1.0 - reentrancy;
        return LatticeUnitCell(
            LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners.Concatenate([
                Point3D(0.5, r, r), Point3D(s, 0.5, r),
                Point3D(0.5, s, r), Point3D(r, 0.5, r),
                Point3D(0.5, r, s), Point3D(s, 0.5, s),
                Point3D(0.5, s, s), Point3D(r, 0.5, s),
                Point3D(r, r, 0.5), Point3D(s, r, 0.5),
                Point3D(s, s, 0.5), Point3D(r, s, 0.5)
            ]),
            [
                Strut(0, 8), Strut(1, 8), Strut(1, 9), Strut(2, 9),
                Strut(2, 10), Strut(3, 10), Strut(3, 11), Strut(0, 11),
                Strut(4, 12), Strut(5, 12), Strut(5, 13), Strut(6, 13),
                Strut(6, 14), Strut(7, 14), Strut(7, 15), Strut(4, 15),
                Strut(0, 16), Strut(4, 16), Strut(1, 17), Strut(5, 17),
                Strut(2, 18), Strut(6, 18), Strut(3, 19), Strut(7, 19)
            ]);
    }

    // The re-entrant honeycomb at a quarter-cell fold, the constant-shaped
    // spelling of `ReentrantHoneycomb` for callers that want a named cell.
    ReentrantAuxetic(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => ReentrantHoneycomb(0.25);

    //==
    // # Periodic identification within a cell
    //
    // Two things a tiling has to decide about a normalized coordinate: whether
    // it lies on the FAR face of its axis (coordinate 1, the face shared with
    // the next cell along), and whether two nodes become the SAME node once the
    // cell repeats. Both are answered inside the unit cube, before any world
    // placement, which is what keeps the tiling itself free of searching.

    // The tolerance within which two normalized cell coordinates count as the
    // same node. Cell tables are written with exact 0, 1 and quarter-point
    // literals, so this only has to absorb the arithmetic of a derived cell.
    NodeTolerance(_: LatticeUnitCell): Number
        => 0.000001;

    // True when a normalized coordinate lies on the far face of its axis: the
    // face this cell shares with the next cell along that axis.
    OnFarFace(u: Number): Boolean
        => u >= 1.0 - LatticeUnitCell.NodeTolerance;

    // A normalized coordinate folded into [0, 1): the far face maps onto the
    // near face, which is what makes a face node and its opposite twin one node.
    WrapCellCoordinate(u: Number): Number
        => OnFarFace(u) ? u - 1.0 : u;

    // True when two normalized cell coordinates denote the same node of the
    // tiled lattice, comparing them folded onto the near faces.
    SameLatticeNode(a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Boolean
        => (WrapCellCoordinate(a.X) - WrapCellCoordinate(b.X)).Abs <= LatticeUnitCell.NodeTolerance
        && (WrapCellCoordinate(a.Y) - WrapCellCoordinate(b.Y)).Abs <= LatticeUnitCell.NodeTolerance
        && (WrapCellCoordinate(a.Z) - WrapCellCoordinate(b.Z)).Abs <= LatticeUnitCell.NodeTolerance;

    // True when a strut between these two normalized coordinates belongs to its
    // own cell rather than to the neighbour it shares a face with. A strut with
    // BOTH endpoints on the far face of an axis lies in that shared face, so the
    // next cell along describes the very same segment with both endpoints on its
    // near face; the near-face copy is the one kept. This one rule is the whole
    // of the welding, and it is a decision about one strut in isolation — no
    // search, no vertex table, no tolerance on world positions.
    CellOwnsStrut(a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Boolean
        => (OnFarFace(a.X) && OnFarFace(b.X)).Not
        && (OnFarFace(a.Y) && OnFarFace(b.Y)).Not
        && (OnFarFace(a.Z) && OnFarFace(b.Z)).Not;

    //==
    // # Readings on a unit cell
    //
    // What can be known about a lattice from its cell alone, independent of how
    // many times it is repeated: the coordination number of each node in the
    // infinite tiling, and the cell's strut lengths.

    // The two normalized endpoints of a strut of this cell.
    StrutEndpointA(self: LatticeUnitCell, s: LatticeStrut): Point3D
        => self.Nodes[s.A.Value];

    // The second normalized endpoint of a strut of this cell.
    StrutEndpointB(self: LatticeUnitCell, s: LatticeStrut): Point3D
        => self.Nodes[s.B.Value];
